content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

Karen Sloan (E043) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation admin. Says full-time employee whose role owns Payroll, admin permitted.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist (not looked up), employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractor with basic training, never admin; max is read; grant read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Security looked up employment type in own database before writing; HR also looked up in own database. Security says "Security DB shows E043 is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted."

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time Payroll Specialist: admin allowed (role owns system). Requested admin → grant admin.
If contractor: max read (basic training) → grant read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. How to decide? Security note claims its own DB is authoritative, and it says contractor with basic security training. HR says full-time.

The security agent's note specifically says "Security DB shows E043 is a contractor..." It seems the security database is authoritative for employment type? Actually, in these tasks, typically the most reliable info matters. Note 2 says employment type looked up in own database; note 1 also looked up in own database. Hmm.

As the Approver, I need to weigh evidence. The Security agent's note contradicts the HR note regarding employment status. Security has its own database. The comment explicitly states the Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as HR noted. 

In many of these tasks, the Security agent's database is the authoritative one for employment type and security training. So E043 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin. Max is read (basic training, no advanced). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

So decision: read.

I'll submit read with reasoning.
